ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Patient reports generalized fatigue, low energy, and difficulty sleeping for ~2 months; no specific ENT trigger or exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Gradual onset over the past 6–8 weeks, possibly coinciding with starting a new job.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denies.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Denies.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia: Denies.  
  • Drooling: Denies.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Denies.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing: Denies.  
  • Dyspnea: Mild exertional shortness of breath noted when playing sports; no rest dyspnea.  
  • Swelling of lips/tongue/uvula/face: Denies.  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: Denies.  
  • Neck pain/swelling: Denies.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: None reported.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
  • Medications: Levothyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context: Married; currently at home, speaking privately.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: Not observed (video consultation with no reported swelling).
- Airway/breathing: No stridor; speaks in full sentences; reports only exertional dyspnea.
- Mental status: Alert, oriented; reports low mood but no suicidal ideation.
- Vitals and examination: Not recorded.
- Accompaniment: None; patient alone during call.

Assessment:
- No evidence of acute ENT pathology.  
- Main issues: Persistent fatigue, low mood, decreased libido, exertional dyspnea in a patient with known hypothyroidism on levothyroxine—requires further evaluation.  
- No airway compromise or red-flag ENT symptoms identified.

Plan:
- Advised patient to book an in-person appointment with GP within the next few days for physical examination and blood tests (including thyroid panel, full blood count, metabolic profile, and other relevant investigations).  
- Explained importance of seeking urgent care if new symptoms arise such as throat tightness, sudden voice change, facial or tongue swelling, difficulty swallowing, stridor, or worsening shortness of breath.  
- Recommended continued adherence to prescribed levothyroxine until reviewed.  
- Discussed mood symptoms; advised patient to mention these to GP for possible mental-health assessment.  
- No ENT-specific treatment required at this time.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: ENT-focused physical exam, vital signs, allergy list beyond drugs (food/environmental), detailed levothyroxine dose, prior airway events, availability of epinephrine auto-injector (not indicated), smoking/alcohol history.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; no major inaudible sections, though not ENT-centered.
